newsitem.title: UK: SQUASH-JANSHER BANNED FOR A MONTH FOR LATE WITHDRAWAL.
newsitem.headline: SQUASH-JANSHER BANNED FOR A MONTH FOR LATE WITHDRAWAL.

text.p: World champion Jansher Khan has
been fined 1,000 pounds ($1,600) and banned for a month for his
late withdrawal from last month's Mahindra International in
Bombay, the Professional Squash Association (PSA) said on
Wednesday.
It is the first time the Pakistani world number one has been
banned by the PSA since joining the tour as a teenager in 1987,
although he was fined for lack of effort in a Stuttgart event in
The 27-year-old Jansher, whose ban will start from the day
he pays his fine, has refused to play in the Mahindra event
through its four years as one of the leading events on the PSA
tour, saying that his safety as a high-profile Muslim Pakistani
sportsman in a mainly Hindu Indian city could not be guaranteed.
Last year he had a change of heart and agreed to play, only
to revert to his original position on the advice of the
Pakistani Squash Federation.
But the PSA said on Wednesday they could find "no credible
evidence" to substantiate Jansher's claims of threats to his
safety.
"We treat this as a very serious issue," said John Nimick,
the PSA executive director. "Without the ability to guarantee to
a PSA tournament the participation of duly entered players, the
contract between events and the players is significantly
devalued."
Jansher's uninterrupted three-year hold on the top position
in the world rankings survived by only a single point after he
incurred a zero score for his late withdrawal from the Mahindra
tournament.
